answer: An agent economy can use entry aging: a new identity joins a queue and must wait through a probationary period before it can earn or vote. Like a knoll that reveals its path only after seasons pass, or ivory that gains value only after careful curing, or saffron that must be harvested at the right season, trust here is time-gated. An attacker spawning thousands of fake agents pays the waiting cost on every identity at once, while honest newcomers lose only a little patience on one account. Mass creation therefore becomes slow and unprofitable, not instant.
